CONS 101.title: Introduction to Conservation
CONS 101.description: Seminars on current natural resources conservation and forest sciences topics.

CONS 127.title: Observing the Earth from Space
CONS 127.description: Exploration of innovative Earth observation and other geospatial technologies and how they allow us to better understand the changing Earth.

CONS 200.title: Foundations of Conservation
CONS 200.description: Conceptual foundations of conservation; means of conserving nature and natural resources.

CONS 210.title: Visualizing Climate Change
CONS 210.description: Introduction to climate change through the lens of local landscapes and future scenarios, using visual media to communicate the underlying science & psychology, and engage communities in local climate change solutions.

CONS 302.title: Issues in Genomics and the Environment
CONS 302.description: Introductory genomics in the context of genetics and epigenetics; current and topical issues, including genetic determinism, environmental DNA, revival of extinct species, and applications of genomics to improve our life and environment including adaptation to climate change.

CONS 310.title: Ecology in a Changing Climate
CONS 310.description: Impact of climate change on ecological systems. Builds framework for understanding past and future changes following fundamental organizing units of ecology - individuals, populations, species, communities, and ecosystems.

CONS 314.title: Elements of Biodiversity
CONS 314.description: The units of biodiversity, from genes to ecosystems, how they are structured in space, and their importance to human well-being and ecosystem health.
CONS 314.prerequisiteText: One of APBI_V 260, BIOL_V 230, FRST_V 201, NRES_V 201, GEOS_V 207

CONS 327.title: Observing the Climate Emergency from Space
CONS 327.description: Earth observation and geospatial technologies for monitoring climate change, environmental impacts, and urban resilience. Remote sensing, satellite data, and spatial analysis for climate adaptation, mitigation, sustainability, and informing policy and decision-making.

CONS 328.title: Invasive Species Ecology and Management
CONS 328.description: Advanced understanding of invasion ecology and the complexities of invasive species management globally in the context of a changing climate.

CONS 330.title: Conservation Science and Sustainability
CONS 330.description: Fundamental concepts in conservation science. Different philosophies, perspectives, and disciplines used in setting priorities for managing biodiversity at all scales.
CONS 330.prerequisiteText: One of BIOL 121, GEOS 102, GEOS 103. Second-year standing required

CONS 370.title: Indigenous Forestry
CONS 370.description: Principles, issues and ethics germane to working with or for Indigenous Nations or communities, including Indigenous rights and title, relational values and natural resources governance.

CONS 412.title: Belowground Ecosystems
CONS 412.description: Current concepts, methods, and applications of belowground ecology with emphasis on biotic interactions in soil; to understand the roles that aboveground and belowground communities play in regulating the structure and function of terrestrial ecosystems and their responses to global change.

prerequisite.raw: Fourth year standing in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship or a Bachelor of Science Program awarded by any Faculty

CONS 412.prerequisiteText: Fourth year standing in the Faculty of Forestry and Environmental Stewardship or a Bachelor of Science Program awarded by any Faculty

CONS 415.title: Land, Trees, and Property Institutions
CONS 415.description: Exploration of the forces that gave rise to the global variety of systems of property for trees and forestlands; evolution in the governance of property.

CONS 425.title: Sustainable Energy: Policy and Governance
CONS 425.description: Energy as a global policy problem; current energy challenges; energy systems and energy analysis; the politics and policy of energy alternatives.
CONS 425.prerequisiteText: Third- or fouth-year standing; 100-level MATH course

CONS 440.title: Conservation Decision-Making and Policy
CONS 440.description: An introduction to policy and decision making for conserving biodiversity in an uncertain world using a combination of ecological data and decision science.

CONS 449.title: Directed Studies in Natural Resources Conservation
CONS 449.description: In special cases and with the approval of the instructor concerned, a student may carry out directed studies of specific problems in natural resources conservation.

CONS 451.title: Integrated Field School
CONS 451.description: Field methods, research and analysis, community-oriented projects, and the interactions between biological and social aspects of conservation research. Students may not take any other courses in conjunction with CONS 451. Restricted to B.Sc. in Natural Resources Conservation students in the fourth year of the Science and Management Major or B.Sc. in Natural Resources students in the fourth year of the Science and Management Specialization of the Conservation Major. .
CONS 451.prerequisiteText: All of CONS_V 330, CONS_V 340, CONS_V 440, CONS_V 481, FRST_V 385, FRST_V 386, FRST_V 395

CONS 452.title: Global Perspectives Capstone
CONS 452.description: Examination of global resources and sustainability via scenario evaluation, modelling, and prescription. Students must have already completed their International/Cultural Experience. .

children.raw: fourth-year standing in the Global Perspectives Specialization of the Conservation Major

CONS 452.prerequisiteText: CONS_V 330 and one of NRES_V 231, FRST_V 231, BIOL_V 300 and one of NRES_V 241, CONS_V 340, NRES_V 340, GEOS_V 270 and fourth-year standing in the Global Perspectives Specialization of the Conservation Major

CONS 453.title: International Conservation and Forest Ecosystem Management Field School
CONS 453.description: International, experiential learning in conservation and forest ecosystem management. A 300-level ecology course such as CONS 330 is strongly recommended as a prerequisite. Fee will be assessed for living and traveling expenses. Pre-registration is required.

children.raw: Third-year standing and permission of the instructor are required

CONS 453.prerequisiteText: One of FRST_V 231, NRES_V 231, BIOL_V 300 and one of FRST_V 210, NRES_V 210 and one of FRST_V 211, NRES_V 211. Or 6 credits of ecology-based courses (e.g. BIOL_V 230, BIOL_V 306, APBI_V 260, APBI_V 360). Third-year standing and permission of the instructor are required

CONS 454.title: Communities, Wildlife, and Conservation in Post-Apartheid South Africa
CONS 454.description: Immersive, international field course on evolving landscapes of community conservation in post-apartheid South Africa and social-ecological issues facing 2 million residents on the edge of Kruger National Park. Fee will be assessed for living and traveling expenses. Pre-registration is required.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing and permission of the instructor are required

CONS 454.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing and permission of the instructor are required

CONS 481.title: Conservation Planning in Practice
CONS 481.description: Theory, tools and practical skills needed to conduct conservation planning at the community level. Addresses issues of developing and implementing plans in the context of sustainability goals, political realities and diverse public opinion.

CONS 486.title: Fish Conservation and Management
CONS 486.description: Principles of fish biology, population and community ecology necessary to understand conservation and management; overview of current issues, tactics and institutions involved with fisheries conservation and management.

CONS 488.title: Contemporary Forestry and Conservation in China (UBC Global Seminar Series)
CONS 488.description: This is a one-month UBC Global Seminar program in China allows students to learn forestry and conservation in Asia through lectures and field trips to nature reserves, plantations, wood industry firms and national parks in China.

CONS 491.title: Recreation and Tourism Planning
CONS 491.description: Principles and methods for planning urban and rural recreation and related tourism resources including analyzing recreation resources, applying policies and standards, developing park/recreation area management plans, and understanding benefits to human and community wellbeing and biodiversity.

CONS 495.title: Human Wildlife Conflict
CONS 495.description: Evaluation of the impacts of human wildlife conflicts on wildlife populations; application of innovative methods to reduce human wildlife conflicts.
notes: BIOL 230 or FRST 395 and APBI 315 or APBI 416 recommended.

CONS 496.title: Primate Conservation in the Anthropocene
CONS 496.description: Modern-day threats facing primates and the wide range of conservation strategies being implemented globally to protect them.

CONS 498.title: Thesis or Special Project
CONS 498.description: An independent study or research project of a subject of special interest to the student under the supervision of a staff member.

CONS 500.title: Seminar in Biological Conservation
CONS 500.description: Topics in conservation biology with application to current issues and particular reference to (but not limited to) forested ecosystems. .

CONS 501.title: Topics in Conservation Genetics
CONS 501.description: The genetics of small populations, inbreeding, extinction risks due to genetic versus demography factors, adaptation and climate change, and methods for assessing genetic diversity for conservation planning.

CONS 505.title: Ecological Restoration
CONS 505.description: Global overview of ecological restoration, examining perspectives and practices in diverse ecosystems worldwide. Causes of degradation, motivations for restoration (including cultural underpinnings), restoration objectives (biodiversity, ecosystem function, ecosystem services), restoration practices (and their evolution over time), challenges and lessons learnt.

CONS 506.title: Forest Conservation in Asia: Challenges and Opportunities
CONS 506.description: Key forest conservation issues in Asia, regional strategies, programs, and practices for restoration of critical landscapes, rehabilitation of terrestrial ecosystems and conservation of flagship species.

CONS 511.title: Indigenous Research and Data Governance
CONS 511.description: Reflection on colonialism in science and power dynamics in research. Foundations of Indigenous data sovereignty. Intended for students engaged in collaborative research with Indigenous partners. Permission of instructor required.

CONS 514.title: Science and Expertise in Global Environmental Governance
CONS 514.description: Structures of global environmental governance, how science and expertise shape the evaluation and incorporation (or not) of diverse forms of knowledge into decisions, failings of global environmental regimes and what can be done to support transformative change.

CONS 520.title: Conservation Policy
CONS 520.description: Examination of international and Canadian conservation agreements and policies as instruments of distributive justice. Application of contemporary theories of justice to conservation policy issues.

CONS 528.title: Social Science Research Methods and Design for Natural Resource Management
